## Description {#details}

<p>This file supports working with JSON data.</p>


<p>It comprises:</p>


<ul class="doxyList ">
<li>classes which hold dynamically-typed parsed JSON structures These are value types that can be composed, inspected, and modified. See json::Value, and the related types json::Object and json::Array.</li>
<li>functions to parse JSON text into Values, and to serialize Values to text. See <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/lib/lib/debuginfo/lib/debuginfo/gsym/linetable-cpp/#a45e99fb329714d8911cb5e116eb8a3bc">parse()</a>, operator&lt;&lt;, and format_provider.</li>
<li>a convention and helpers for mapping between json::Value and user-defined types. See fromJSON(), ObjectMapper, and the class comment on Value.</li>
<li>an output API json::OStream which can emit JSON without materializing all structures as json::Value.</li>
</ul>

<p>Typically, JSON data would be read from an external source, parsed into a Value, and then converted into some native data structure before doing real work on it. (And vice versa when writing).</p>


<p>Other serialization mechanisms you may consider:</p>


<ul class="doxyList ">
<li>YAML is also text-based, and more human-readable than JSON. It's a more complex format and data model, and YAML parsers aren't ubiquitous. <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/include/include/llvm/include/llvm/support/yamlparser-h">YAMLParser.h</a> is a streaming parser suitable for parsing large documents (including JSON, as YAML is a superset). It can be awkward to use directly. YAML I/O (<a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/include/include/llvm/include/llvm/support/yamltraits-h">YAMLTraits.h</a>) provides data mapping that is more declarative than the toJSON/fromJSON conventions here.</li>
<li>LLVM bitstream is a space- and CPU- efficient binary format. Typically it encodes LLVM IR ("bitcode"), but it can be a container for other data. Low-level reader/writer libraries are in Bitstream/Bitstream*.h</li>
</ul>
